subject.title: In-turn background work (Workflow / run_in_background / Workflow-backed skills) is SIGKILLed at the turn boundary under the claude-cli runtime

question: Should claude-cli longwork remain limited to OpenClaw-owned durable background surfaces, or should OpenClaw support detached Workflow/native background jobs with persisted origin and completion delivery?
rationale: Both choices are plausible and affect runtime ownership, user-visible tool affordances, and message/session delivery semantics; source inspection cannot decide the intended product contract.

options.title: Keep Unsupported Affordances Refused
options.body: Continue denying claude-cli native background tools and only expose longwork through OpenClaw-owned surfaces until durable survival plus delivery is designed.

options.title: Add Durable Background Host
options.body: Implement a persistent host for approved Workflow/native longwork and persist origin/completion events before user-visible delivery.

options.title: Document Non-Goal
options.body: Close the remaining Workflow/native background expectation as unsupported and document the supported OpenClaw alternatives.

recommendation.title: Keep Unsupported Affordances Refused
recommendation.body: Continue denying claude-cli native background tools and only expose longwork through OpenClaw-owned surfaces until durable survival plus delivery is designed.

likelyOwner.reason: The Claude live-session lifecycle was introduced through their PR and this decision centers on that runtime boundary.
